newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat sees limit falls in slow Hungary mkt.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat sees limit falls in slow Hungary mkt.

text.p: Grains futures prices tended lower on Thursday on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) with milling wheat continuing its limit falls, traders said.

Milling wheat prices dropped by the daily allowed 400 forints limit for all maturities, ending at 24,300 forints per tonne for May, 21,200 for August, 21,500 for September and 22,600 forints for December.

"There are two reasons for the falls," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle. "Current Budapest prices of $117 to $120 per tonne will not be applicable to the export quota prices to be announced soon, and there is also a technical correction as the market is sharply overbought."
Maize prices were unchanged for most maturities except for July which lost 250 at 17,240 forints and November, which finished at 18,500, up 90.
Herczeg said that unlike milling wheat most maize supplies were with producers rather than in warehouses, as producers were holding out for better prices.
"Holding onto supplies is not going to work, I'm afraid," he said. "Once the May season of warehouse clearing comes they will have to release stocks and they will not get the prices they want."
Total turnover was a meagre 739 lots or 336.2 million forints.
